items.title: Ellen Rowe interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, December 2, 2024
items.q: if somebody is in love with, you know, Brian Blade’s music

ctx.x: That is an excellent question. Yeah, I think about that a good bit. I mean especially my faculty colleagues and I, if they’re over the age of 50 we find ourselves definitely questioning some things that we took for granted when we were first starting out to teach. And I’d say one of the big ones is that I think when I started at U Conn there’s still pretty much a tried and true way for young students to, you know, get their feet wet and go to the jam sessions that existed at the time, to point them towards…

and I mean it still is in the sense that if somebody is in love with, you know, Brian Blade’s music and you know we’re certainly going to say hey go to all his gigs and try and get to know him and his players. But I think we are aware that students are learning, they are finding different paths and there’s so much entrepreneurship involved now because there’s so many different ways that students can get their music out there, can connect with other students, you know ways of creating their music that’s very…

Could I zone in on a word you used, “integrity.” What did you mean by that? I was interested to learn when I interviewed Randy Brecker that much of what he does now is he stays at home and people send him tracks and he plays various solos on them.
